description_full: Xiaomi Corporation, an investment holding company, engages in the development and sales of smartphones in Mainland China and internationally. It operates through Smartphones, IoT and Lifestyle Products, Internet Services, and smart electric vehicles segments. The company also offers internet of things (IoT) and lifestyle products comprising smart large home appliances, smart TVs, tablets, wearables and other IoT and lifestyle products; hardware repairment services for products; installation services for certain IoT products; and sale of materials. In addition, it provides internet services, such as advertising, online game, and fintech services; and development, manufacture, and sales of smart electric vehicles. Further, the company in the wholesale and retail of smartphones and ecosystem partners' products; investment activities; sales of smart hardware; software and hardware development; procurement and sales of smartphones, ecosystem partners' products and spare parts, and raw materials; operation of retail stores; and commercial factoring and e-commerce business. Additionally, it provides intra-group capital supervision, collection, remittance, credit guarantee, and interest rate risk management; customer; software related; promotion; electronic payment technology; and technical services. Xiaomi Corporation was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 52K people. Revenue per employee of $1.3M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $61K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $15K per employee reflects an ownership culture. Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10). R&D investment of 7% of revenue (moderate) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: Xiaomi Corp. is a large-cap technology business with a $99.1B market cap on $68.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 21% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $3.2B in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.82× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 8.7×.

Net dilution runs at 5.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 39% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 0.87, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.07 vs 5y 0.79), so read it loosely.

The price implies 5.6% annual cash-flow growth, 5pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 15% earns above the cost of capital of 9.0%, but the 6pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.50).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $9.9B.

own: Insiders own 20.5%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 27%.
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-5.0%), diluting holders.
people: With about 52,876 employees, each generates about $1.3M of revenue, 3.5x the Technology median.
That works out to $61K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
